_: Authored half of the final-cut read. The scene rows come from the platform's scene analysis when it returns; everything else is read from the project's own record — favourites, the post-deadline jobs, the uploads, the Predictor. Regenerate the page with design/build-final-cut.py.
intro: The board closed at 22:53 UTC on deadline day with 27 cards and a 5:43 plan. The delivered film is 6:17, and the platform's scene analysis of the Sep 16 master reads it as 108 scenes — a hundred of them the film, eight of them the festival packshot that runs in front of it. Against a plan of 23 shots at 13 seconds, the cut runs at 3.7 seconds a scene: it is the film the thesis chapter's second ribbon warned against, and it plays anyway, because the long holds survived exactly where the writing was and the rest was cut to two songs. This chapter reads the picture against the two scene-clip artefacts the cut was made from — shot-board.html and the Canvas Boards page — and against the project's own record of favourites, post-deadline jobs and uploads, and turns the differences into rules.

diff.board: 23 shots at 13.0s (bible) · 27 cards at 12.7s (board). A held frame as the signature.
diff.cut: 100 scenes in 6:08 of film, mean 3.7s, median 3s. Seven holds over 9s: S1 (15), S4 (13), the kill beat (13), the fish (12), S3 (11), the end card (10), the dragon's flight (9).
diff.why: The doctrine of the held frame lost to the need for coverage. One generation per shot gave the editor one angle; the timeline wanted three, and got them from takes the board had never admitted. The holds that survived are the ones the writing had earned.

diff.board: Frame one is F01, near-black, an ember at the base.
diff.cut: Nine seconds of the platform's packshot — the festival's gold star, its UI, a samurai — before the aerial over the Sun.
diff.why: MVS component 1, placed by the submit flow at the head. The jury's first nine seconds are not yours. Check whether the flow allows the packshot at the tail; if not, budget for it.

diff.board: f84a308f, 30s, on the current courtyard element.
diff.cut: A 15s aerial over ochre cloud and a ring of white pillars, under piano and cello. Then a night jungle river that is on no board.
diff.why: The favourites said the older crane pair; the picture says the ring of pillars, held 15s, and then a cutaway to a planet. The Sun reads as a place in cloud, and from scene 24 on as a temple on an island at night.

diff.board: Five shots, 1:25, the first 34 seconds without a cut.
diff.cut: 1:58 and 33 scenes, 3.6s each — a montage of close-ups (a foot on stone, a point of light in the brow, a collar of light, fires along the cracks) from at least three Oriane designs, none of them the v3 sheet, before the dialogue arrives at 1:28.
diff.why: Twenty of the 33 scenes are on no board. The cut reached back past the admission window for coverage the plan never generated. It is the most re-cut movement in the film and the one furthest from the bible.

diff.cut: 11s · 13s+1s · 7s. All three lines survive verbatim; 'I know.' is its own cut.
diff.why: The dialogue held longest of anything in the film. The trims came off the takes' ends, not their heads — the lines start at once.

diff.board: The bookend: Caedom alone on the Sun, the last shot before the end card, with the two V.O. lines from the opening.
diff.cut: At 2:04, as the act-out of Movement I: Caedom walks away toward the moon past the orbs under 'tired to the bone and unbroken — he could erase everything', fade to black, then 'there must be risk…' over a garden shot and the 108-years card.
diff.why: The film does not return to the Sun. The bookend became the hinge into the storm, and both V.O. lines went with it. The ending was found somewhere else (see the coda).

diff.cut: 2:02–2:17: the gem on the floor, a crystal rolling down gold, the card, a crystalline blue mass zooming out. 15s across four scenes.
diff.why: The transition the board argued against is the film's hinge, and it carries the title card and the change of music.

diff.board: Nine shots, 118s, two point-of-view changes, the climax silent from orbit.
diff.cut: 2:07–4:14, 27 scenes, under a metal song with lyrics. Two leviathans: the skeletal dragon with the rider in red (23s, 2:37–3:00 — the pair the board excluded for the wrong element) and the grey beast (3:15–3:50, 4:10). Two vortex passages (4:03 and 4:25–4:39), both under lyrics.
diff.why: The excluded takes were the set piece. The Predictor's best data in the account was the dark-ground storm, and the cut agrees; the silence rule did not survive a song that peaks on 'In the sky!' over the eye of the storm.

diff.cut: 3:23–3:33: she runs the creature's back and fights the figures rising from its skin, in the battle suit — the Sep 14 regeneration.
diff.why: Made at 23:04 on deadline night, favourited, and used. The one regeneration that changed the picture.

diff.cut: Two passages: the kill beat on the creature's head (3:50–4:03, 13s) and, after the song ends, the sphere of blue light with the Turned watching (4:16–4:25, 9s, the favourited blend take), ending on the knowing smile the NEW-1 prompt asked for.
diff.why: S12 became two shots and carried NEW-1's beat. The 'mind divides' was never rendered as written; its expression arrived inside another take.

diff.board: 15s silent from orbit; then 13s intimate, upside-down, the Stone thrown, the empty frame held.
diff.cut: S13 twice (6s + 14s) under lyrics. S14 as 11s across six scenes: red eyes on golden cloud, a burst of light beneath her, the upside-down face (1s), the cloud with a face and red eyes, golden wings. No Stone thrown; no empty frame.
diff.why: The upside-down face — the shot as written — lasts one second. The dark cloud of Option D is literal and has eyes. The two beats the bible called the film's stake (the empty frame) and its hinge (the Stone leaving) are not in the picture; the streak is.

diff.cut: NEW-4 at 4:50 (4s of 16); NEW-2 at 5:25–5:32 (7s, the island of rock over the fleet and its fall); NEW-1 not identifiable as rendered.
diff.why: Two of the three additions made it, cut to a quarter of their length. The third, the intimate sacrifice, was absorbed into S12.

diff.board: Change 1: the brothers' first five seconds before the vortex.
diff.cut: The brothers first appear at 4:59 (the swim) and 5:06 (the beach). Nothing before the vortex.
diff.why: The zero-generation fix was not made. The film meets the brothers cold, at 4:59, with 78 seconds left.

diff.board: Nine shots, 108s; a 14s unbroken mountain; the only push-in on Alder's face.
diff.cut: 4:54–5:42, 48s, 15 scenes at 3.2s. The ships read as jagged rocks against the red disc (the B lane), the boys run (3s), the Keepers walk (5s), the doors close (3s) and open (3s), the kneel and the rise (3s), the mound (4s + 3s), one Keeper kneels (3s), the brothers in the grass (7s, the dark cloud by the sun).
diff.why: The miracle plays in ten seconds across three cuts. The thesis shot is 7s. The doctrine of the locked-off witness became the fastest-cut minute in the film.

diff.board: The swim in silhouette, two adults.
diff.cut: 4:59–5:03: two small swimmers over the reef. The analyser reads them as toddlers; at 5:06 as young boys; at 5:35 as young men.
diff.why: The 18+ rule. The sheets say nineteen and eighteen; the wide takes read younger to a machine and may to a juror. A re-render of the swim with the adult sheets attached, or the wide only, is the fix.

diff.board: S23 then the end card: the tear as a point of light on the floor.
diff.cut: 5:42–6:02: a mountain peak in morning light, a crater lake from above, its surface, under it, and 12 seconds of silver fish rising toward the light. Then 5s of black, then 10s of Oriane's face in a metal collar with a beam of light scanning her eyes.
diff.why: An ending the board never had: a rise toward light, a breath of black, a look to camera. It reads as a prelude's ending — open, and pointed at what comes next — and it was found on the timeline.

diff.board: No score under dialogue; silence at the climax; three sound worlds.
diff.cut: Piano and cello for the Sun; a metal song for the storm ('Deep in the mountains… I was the light, the memory of one… the seasons change'); an orchestral-rock song from the ascension to the end ('Is this destiny… stars in the sky… don't make it stop now… I'm still here to see how'). Cuts land on lyrics.
diff.why: The film is cut to its songs. That is a genre decision the board never made, and it explains the rhythm: a lyric video for a novel, with a two-minute dialogue scene inside it.

diff.cut: c0bdbe0e is a 15-second leviathan clip in a teal wave under a red sky, not the film. bd28d7c2 is the same 15-second leviathan clip — its analysis completed on Sep 30 with eight scenes and 0:15. The only full cut in the account is the Sep 16 MOV.
diff.why: The 'low and HQ' on the Downloads drive were never uploaded. The master in the project is the version this read is of.

feel.t: It cut like the film the bible warned against, and it plays
feel.p: A hundred scenes at 3.7 seconds against a plan of twenty-three at thirteen. The holds survived where the writing was: the aerial over the Sun, the three dialogue shots, the kill beat, the fish. Everything else is montage cut to two songs, and the montage is what gives the film pace where single generations gave it none.

Piano for the Sun, metal for the storm, an orchestral-rock song from the ascension to the end. The cuts land on lyrics — 'Stars in the sky' over the kneel, 'Don't make it stop now' over the brothers, 'In the sky!' over the eye of the storm. The silent climax was not kept. This is a music film with a dialogue scene inside it, and once you hear it that way the edit makes sense.

feel.t: The Sun is an island at night
feel.p: Movement I's place reads as a temple of light on a night island with a moon and a planet, not the surface of a star. The gold plate survived as a colour and as the fire along the cracks; the ochre cloud and the ring of pillars at the top are the only frames that say 'star'.

A white light-grid dress, a collar of light, the black suit with gold lines, the red gown on the dragon, the green battle suit, the yellow-piped suit in the sphere. The Predictor could not see it and the analyser describes each one plainly. A continuity audit on the timeline would have caught it; the audit only ever ran on the board.

feel.t: The bookend became a hinge, and the ending was found underwater
feel.p: Caedom's walk away and both V.O. lines close Movement I at 2:04; the film never returns to the Sun. It ends on a mountain lake, a descent under the surface, twelve seconds of fish rising toward light, five seconds of black, and Oriane's face looking into the lens. Open, forward, a prelude's ending — better than the loop the board planned, and nobody planned it.

Movement III runs 48 seconds. The ships read as beasts against the red disc (the B lane the bible wrote and the board never picked), the Keepers walk, the doors close and open, the mass rises, the mound hangs and falls, one Keeper kneels, the brothers get seven seconds with the dark cloud by the sun. The locked-off witness became the fastest-cut minute in the film.

Anderson gets the dragon — 23 seconds of a skeletal leviathan taking flight under a guitar solo, the set piece the board excluded. Papamichael gets the aerial, the three dialogue holds and the fish. Catmull gets seven seconds of the brothers and a dark cloud by the sun, which is the film's idea, cut to the length of a lyric.

grade.p: The analyser's palettes: gold and night-blue for the Sun; purple storm with cyan water walls, red energy on the dragon and green bioluminescence for the storm; red disc and pink haze for the island; dark red and purple for the fall of the mound; pale morning blue and clear teal for the coda. Movement II is not desaturated — it carries four accents.

grade.t: Pull Movement II to one accent
grade.p: Keep the purple sky. Pull the dragon's red veins and the green glow toward the cyan of the water walls so the storm is one world with one light in it. The eye of the storm then reads as the absence of that light, which is what the board wanted from silence.

grade.t: The ascension is the one seam
grade.p: 4:15–4:50 goes cold blue (the sphere), then gold cloud, then teal dusk, then the sunset streak. Match the gold-cloud shots to the streak that follows: warm the dusk, hold the blacks. It is the only stretch where the grade changes world inside a sequence.

grade.t: Leave the island and the coda
grade.p: Movement III is already one world — a red disc, pink haze, dark red for the fall. The coda's morning blue is the only cool daylight in the film and reads as a new day. Both are right; level-match and stop.

grade.t: Blacks are true; the proxy must keep them
grade.p: The analyser reads pitch black behind the end card and near-monochrome brown-black in the spiral. Do not lift the blacks for the low proxy; a lifted black is the first thing a cinematographer sees on a laptop.

grade.t: Grade the takes, then audit the timeline
grade.p: Selection was the grade on this film. On the next one, run the continuity audit on the assembled timeline, not the board — five Orianes and two leviathans reached the cut and every one was a look decision the board never saw.

three_changes.t: Change 1 · the brothers' first five seconds before the vortex
three_changes.p: The brothers first appear at 4:59, after both vortex passages. The zero-generation fix was not made; the film meets them cold with 78 seconds left.

three_changes.t: Change 2 · cut on the tail; S22 on the chroma take
three_changes.p: The dialogue takes lose their ends, not their heads — every line starts at once. S22 is the sunset take with the dark cloud by the sun, held 7s of 12.

three_changes.t: Change 3 · the S1 narration under black; NEW-2 the one generation worth starting
three_changes.p: No narration at the head: the film opens on the packshot, then the aerial under piano. Caedom's 'there must be risk' was used at 2:07 as the hinge instead. NEW-2 was generated Sep 15 and is in the cut at 5:25–5:32.

work_note: Fifteen jobs between the board closing and the Sep 16 upload. Four on deadline night, ten the following evening, one splice at 23:02. The picture confirms which mattered: the S11 regeneration (3:23), Transition A (2:02), Transition B (4:50), the mound (5:25) and the S12 blend take (4:16) are in the cut; the S7 and S10 regenerations and the 'mind divides' takes are not identifiable in it. ♥ marks the ones the cut favourited.
fav_note: Favourites are the cut's own record and the only one the platform keeps, and the picture agrees with them where they exist: every favourited take that can be identified is in the film. Where nothing is favourited — nine shots in the middle of Movement II — the picture shows takes from outside the board altogether.

lessons.t: The board planned 23 shots at 13 seconds; the cut ran 100 at 3.7
lessons.w: The doctrine of the held frame assumed one generation per shot would be held. On the timeline one generation gave the editor one angle, and the film wanted three, so the cut reached back into takes the board had never admitted and cut them to the songs.
lessons.r: Plan coverage or plan montage, but decide. If the film is to hold, generate the B lane and the multi-shot lane for every dialogue and set-piece shot before Gate D. If it is to be cut to music, write the board for it and lock the song first.

lessons.t: The score was three songs, and the edit followed the lyrics
lessons.w: Piano, a metal track, an orchestral-rock track. The cuts land on the words; the vortex plays under 'In the sky!'. The bible's own Reuse page says a music video locks timing to the track before Gate C. It applied, and nobody knew it did.
lessons.r: If there is any chance the sound will be a song, lock the song before the stills reel and cut the reel to it. A silence rule cannot survive a lyric that lands on the climax.

lessons.t: The excluded takes were the set piece
lessons.w: The board excluded the dragon pair for the wrong element. The cut gave them 23 seconds under a guitar solo, the longest sequence in the film, and used the real leviathan beside them as a second beast.
lessons.r: Admit by cast for the record, but never hide a take from the board. Show the excluded ones greyed with the reason; the editor decides what a wrong element costs at the shot's size.

lessons.w: S23 and both V.O. lines were moved to 2:04 as the exit from the Sun. The film ends on a rise underwater, black, and a look to camera that no board contained.
lessons.r: Write the ending on the board as two options — the loop and the open door — and price both. An ending found on the timeline is worth more than one defended on paper, but only if the board has left room for it.

lessons.t: Five Orianes and two leviathans reached the cut
lessons.w: Six costume states of the lead across the film, four of them from sheets the board had retired; two different beasts for one creature. The Predictor cannot see identity; the continuity audit ran on the board and never on the timeline.
lessons.r: Run the continuity audit on the assembled timeline at Gate E, before sound. The audit's unit is the seam, not the take.

lessons.t: The swim reads as children to a machine
lessons.w: The analyser describes the reef swimmers as toddlers and the beach runners as young boys, then the grass shot as young men. The sheets say nineteen and eighteen; the wide takes do not carry the age.
lessons.r: Treat the 18+ rule as a per-take check on wides and silhouettes, not a per-sheet check. Attach the adult sheets to every shot that shows the brothers small, and read each one back through the analyser before delivery.

lessons.t: Nine seconds of packshot before frame one
lessons.w: The submit flow placed the festival bumper at the head of the file: the gold star, the platform's UI, a samurai. The jury's first nine seconds belong to the platform.
lessons.r: Check where the flow puts the packshot before the last export. If it must lead, treat the first nine seconds as not yours and make frame ten the opening.

lessons.t: The film was still being made two days after the deadline, and the 'HQ' in the account is not the film
lessons.w: Six new takes, six regenerations and a splice on Sep 15; the MOV into the project on Sep 16; two Sep 18 uploads, one of which is a fifteen-second leviathan clip. The full cut exists in the account exactly once.
lessons.r: Write down which file was submitted and which is in the project, by id, on the day. Upload the delivered master and its proxy under names that say so, and nothing else to the project root.

lessons.t: Favourites are partial, and the analyser is slow
lessons.w: Nine shots had no favourite; the scene analysis of a 6:17 file took 59 minutes to leave the queue and two of three had returned within the hour.
lessons.r: Favourite the pick of every shot as you lay it. Start the analyser the day the master exists, and read the favourites while it runs.

verdict: What the cut says about the board. The scene-clip artefacts were right about what to hold — the aerial, the three lines, the kill beat, the brothers — and wrong about everything between. The editor cut a music film: a hundred scenes to two songs, with a two-minute dialogue scene held inside it, a 23-second dragon the board had excluded as its set piece, and an ending under water that no board contained. Of the three changes recommended with an hour left, one was applied, one half, one not at all. None of that is a failure of the board; it is what a board is for — a proposal the timeline overrules on sight. The failure is that the board did not know it was overruled: the continuity audit never ran on the timeline, so five Orianes and a second beast reached the jury, and the swim reads as children to a machine. That is what the ninth stage on the Anchorframe desk now does — upload the master, run the scenes, read them against the board, and write every delta back as a lesson, a reminder, and an example. The next film starts from these rows.
